handoff.purpose: LowIntegrityLog class (properties, close, context manager), open_low_append_log, and helper functions for token integrity.

symbols.name: LowIntegrityLog.close
symbols.note: Closes handles _handle and _verify via CloseHandle, sets _closed=True.

symbols.name: open_low_append_log
symbols.note: Creates and labels a log file, returns LowIntegrityLog instance.

symbols.name: _token_integrity_sid
symbols.note: Reads integrity level from a token handle.

symbols.name: _low_integrity_token
symbols.note: Creates a duplicate of current token with Low integrity level.

claims.text: The file is created EMPTY by this process (Medium) and then labelled, so a Low child can neither pre-create it nor choose its contents.
claims.why: Code creates file with open(target, 'wb') (empty) then calls label_low_integrity_file(target).

claims.text: The label is then read back off the opened handle, so what is verified is the object the child will actually write to and not a path that may since have moved.
claims.why: The reading back is done in LowIntegrityLog.__init__ (not in this chunk); code here only creates label then returns LowIntegrityLog(target) which presumably reads label.

claims.text: Lowering your own token needs no privilege; raising one does. That asymmetry is why this works unattended and without admin.
claims.why: Code uses DuplicateTokenEx and SetTokenInformation (not shown) without requiring privilege; no admin elevation is used.

claims.text: The level is READ BACK afterwards: an attestation that says 'Low' because SetTokenInformation returned TRUE is a claim, and this module only ships facts.
claims.why: The read-back is not shown in this chunk; function ends after ConvertStringSidToSidW.

observations.what: LowIntegrityLog properties are simple accessors with no side effects.
close method attempts to close both _handle and _verify; if _verify is not a valid handle, CloseHandle may fail silently.
open_low_append_log checks if file exists before creating; race condition possible.
_token_integrity_sid uses ctypes buffers and casts; potential memory issues if size is incorrect.
_low_integrity_token requests TOKEN_ADJUST_SESSIONID which may require special privilege.
